newsitem.title: USA: CSCE July coffee surges to new 20-year high.
newsitem.headline: CSCE July coffee surges to new 20-year high.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures rose sharply Wednesday morning, with the July contract surging to the highest level in 20 years, as speculative came in buying amid weather forecasts calling for cooler temperatures later this week in top-grower Brazil, traders said.
Although no damaging cold weather is indicated, traders said even the hint of below normal temperatures was enough to spark nervous buying.
"There's talk of cool weather at the end of the week," said one floor trader. "It's all specs buying here and I don't see any selling of consequence."

Benchmark July soared to a new life-of-contract high of 285.00 cents a lb -- a level not seen since 1977. At 0946, July stood at 284.00 cents, up 9.70 cents. Second-month September was 9.50 higher at 247.00, while the back months were up 4.00 to 6.00.

Coffee prices headed higher at the outset, defying pre-opening expectations, a traders followed through on Tuesday's explosive rally. Although traders noted the market was due for a technical correction, they said market sentiment remained extremely bullish.
The latest weather outlooks, which predicted below normal temperatures later this week, also fueled buying.

Weather Services Corp said in its daily comment on Wednesday "somewhat cooler than normal temperatures are expected in the coffee belt this week. However, not damaging cold is indicated as there are no major cold airmasses forecast to build out of Argentina."
WSC said temperatures at the end of the week would only fall to the 40s to low 50s F (5-12 C) -- not nearly cold enough to produce any damage.
"The market is breaking new highs on the charts and looks so bullish, people will pick up on anything," said one market source. "There is a lot of misleading information."
Traders also said the lack of certified coffee stocks pending grading was viewed as bullish.
After Tuesday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were unchanged, at 49,712 60-kg bags as of May 23. There was no coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
